title: NIYYAH is here.
caption: NIYYAH is a calm Qur'an learning companion built for reading, understanding, reflection, and private Circles. The beta is free. Link in bio.

title:
Read less.
Understand more.
caption: You do not need to finish a whole surah today. Start with one ayah, understand what you can, and return gently.

title: Free means free.
caption: The core Qur'an learning experience is free in NIYYAH's beta. No guilt, no fake urgency, and no paywall around understanding the Qur'an.

title:
You do not need
an hour.
caption: Busy day? Open the ayah you left, take one small action, and close with intention.

title:
Context changes
how you read.
caption: Context can change the way a surah opens up. NIYYAH begins with an overview and only shows reviewed revelation context where it is available.

title:
Listen without
leaving the app.
caption: Verified recitation stays inside the reading experience so you can listen without losing your place.

title:
What if Qur'an study
felt less lonely?
caption: NIYYAH Circles are private spaces for family, friends, classes, and MSAs. No public feed. No follower count. Just learning together.

title:
Your family group chat,
but with intention.
caption: One shared ayah can start a meaningful family conversation. Who would you invite first?

title: MSA idea:
caption: MSA challenge: choose one short surah, make a seven-day Circle, and check in together without rankings.

title:
For a Qur'an app,
trust comes first.
caption: A Qur'an app should tell you where its content comes from. NIYYAH keeps source material and educational tools clearly separated.

title:
We would rather
leave it out than guess.
caption: Where attributed source tafsir is unavailable, NIYYAH leaves it out. It does not invent source tafsir or pretend an educational summary is one.

title:
Recitation should not
be generated.
caption: Qur'an recitation in NIYYAH uses verified reciter audio, never a generic AI voice.

title:
Some reflections
are meant to stay private.
caption: Your reflection does not have to become a post. NIYYAH's journal is private by default.

title:
One ayah.
One honest question.
caption: Sometimes one honest question is enough to help an ayah stay with you.

title:
Your spiritual notes
are not content.
caption: Private journals, duas, and reflections should be treated with care, not turned into engagement content.

title:
Do not just save words.
Return to them.
caption: Save one Qur'anic word while you read, then return to it later. Small vocabulary growth adds up.

title:
A quiz should reveal
what to revisit.
caption: NIYYAH quizzes are light understanding checks, not spiritual rankings.

title:
Follow a path
when you feel stuck.
caption: When you do not know where to begin, a guided Learning Journey gives you one clear next step.

title:
Missing a day is not
the end.
caption: Missed a day? You did not fail. NIYYAH is designed to help you continue without shame.

title:
See progress without
turning worship into a game.
caption: Progress can be visible without becoming competitive. Keep a gentle record of what you have read, learned, and reflected on.

title:
Open. Continue.
Close with intention.
caption: NIYYAH brings you back to what matters: the ayah, the reflection, and the next small action.

title:
Create a Circle
in under a minute.
caption: Create a Circle, choose a simple purpose, and invite people you trust.

title:
A code is all
they need.
caption: No audience needed. Share a private Circle code or QR invitation with the people you actually want to learn with.

title:
Accountability without
a leaderboard.
caption: Accountability can sound like: 'our Circle showed up today.' It does not need a leaderboard.

title:
I built the app
I wanted to open.
caption: I started building NIYYAH because I wanted a Qur'an app that felt calm, careful, and easy to return to.

title:
Built with Muslim
students in mind.
caption: NIYYAH is built for Muslim students, families, friends, teachers, and small groups trying to understand the Qur'an together.

title:
Found something wrong?
Tell us directly.
caption: If you find a typo, citation issue, bug, or unclear explanation, NIYYAH gives you a direct way to report it. Correction builds trust.

title:
This would usually
be five different apps.
caption: Reading, context, reflection, vocabulary, progress, quizzes, journeys, and Circles in one calm learning companion. Free beta.

title: Choose your person.
caption: Think of one person who would help you return to the Qur'an this week. Send this to them.

title: Ready when you are.
caption: NIYYAH is ready for its free beta: read, listen, understand, reflect, and learn with people you trust. Link in bio.

title:
Your next step
should be obvious.
caption: Open NIYYAH and continue where you left off. The dashboard brings your current ayah, saved words, and reflection back into view. Continue in one tap.

title:
Before the ayah,
meet the surah.
caption: Begin with context before moving into detail. Use the overview to notice themes and reviewed learning notes before reading. Start with the whole picture.

title:
A complete study flow
inside one screen.
caption: Read, listen, understand, and reflect. Move through one ayah without collecting a pile of open tabs. Try the full flow once.

title:
Your best friend can be
your Qur'an Circle.
caption: One shared goal can make returning easier. Create a private Circle for two people and begin with one short surah. Send the first invitation.

title:
Family study can happen
across different cities.
caption: A private Circle keeps the intention shared. Invite siblings, cousins, or parents and choose one small learning goal together. Bring your family together.

title:
A calmer way for
classrooms to learn.
caption: Use a private Circle for a class, youth group, or MSA. Keep the group focused on reading, reflection, and shared progress without a public feed. Share this with an educator.

title:
Do not just say
'verified.' Show the source.
caption: Trust grows when attribution is visible. NIYYAH separates source material from educational notes and explains its content approach. Open Sources & Trust.

title:
Correction is not
embarrassing.
caption: It is how a trustworthy Qur'an app improves. Users can report content issues, unclear wording, and broken citations directly. Tell us what needs attention.

title:
A learning summary
is not tafsir.
caption: The difference should always be clear. Educational tools support study while attributed source tafsir remains separately labelled. Know what you are reading.

title:
Press play.
Stay with the ayah.
caption: Recitation belongs inside the reading experience. Listen without being pushed into a separate browser or losing your place. Listen inside NIYYAH.

title: Pause should mean pause.
caption: Audio controls should feel predictable. Stop, continue, or move to another ayah while the app keeps the reading flow clear. Read at your own pace.

title:
Listen and read
side by side.
caption: Let the recitation support careful attention. Arabic text, translation, and verified reciter audio stay connected in the ayah flow. Open one ayah with sound.

title:
Reflection needs
more than one doorway.
caption: Meaning, heart, action, and dua invite different kinds of thought. Choose a gentle prompt instead of facing an empty page. Pick the mode you need today.

title: Private by default.
caption: Sharing should be a choice, never a pressure. Write a short reflection for yourself without posting it to an audience. Keep the moment yours.

title:
Your journal should help
you return, not perform.
caption: Saved reflections stay organized by the learning moment. Revisit what an ayah brought up without turning the entry into social content. Return to an old reflection.

title:
Save the word
while it is in context.
caption: Vocabulary begins inside the ayah. Keep meaningful Qur'anic words connected to the reading moment where you found them. Save one word.

title:
Your own Qur'anic
word collection.
caption: Build a vocabulary list from what you actually read. Favorite important words and return to them without copying notes across apps. Build your first collection.

title:
Review should feel
small enough to begin.
caption: A few saved words can become a steady practice. Use short review moments to strengthen recognition over time. Review for two minutes.

title:
A quiz is a mirror,
not a ranking.
caption: Use it to notice what stayed with you. Short questions help reveal what you understood and what deserves another look. Check, then revisit.

title:
Wrong answer?
Return to the lesson.
caption: Learning matters more than the score. NIYYAH keeps the next step connected to understanding instead of competition. Try the question again.

title: Finish with clarity.
caption: Completion should point back to what you learned. A light completion moment helps close the session without turning study into hype. Complete one short quiz.

title:
When you do not know
what to study next.
caption: Choose a guided Learning Journey. Structured themes give you a clear starting point and a manageable next step. Choose a path.

title:
Short sessions.
A connected direction.
caption: A Journey keeps separate learning moments moving together. Return to the theme without rebuilding your study plan every day. Continue the next step.

title:
Progress without
rushing the meaning.
caption: A Journey is a guide, not a race. Move at a pace that supports understanding and honest reflection. Take the time you need.

title:
Strong days matter
even after a pause.
caption: Lifetime engagement should not disappear. NIYYAH keeps a gentle record of the days you showed up without shaming the days you did not. Return today.

title: Paused is not zero.
caption: A missed day does not erase the relationship. Continue the ayah when you are ready instead of facing a punishment screen. Pick it back up gently.

title:
Your Circle showed up
this week.
caption: Shared consistency can encourage without ranking. Notice group presence and small returns while keeping spirituality out of a leaderboard. Encourage the Circle.

title: Remember my place.
caption: That should be the app's job. NIYYAH saves the current learning point so you can spend less time navigating back. Continue where you stopped.

title: Remember my Circle.
caption: Return to the people you were learning with. Keep the last Circle and its shared purpose close to the home flow. Continue together.

title: Remember my last action.
caption: Read, reflected, listened, or made dua. A clear return point makes a small daily connection easier to repeat. Take the next action.

title: Start a Circle.
caption: Name it for the reason you are gathering. Choose family, friends, campus, classroom, or creator-style learning and keep it private. Create yours.

title: Join with a code.
caption: No public profile search required. Enter a trusted invitation code and join the group you were actually invited to. Ask for the code.

title:
Invite without
building an audience.
caption: Private sharing fits private learning. Use the Circle invitation flow instead of asking people to follow another account. Invite one trusted person.

title: Begin with intention.
caption: A Circle session should know why it is meeting. Set a small purpose before opening the reading and reflection flow. Name the intention.

title:
One shared prompt
can open a real discussion.
caption: Keep the conversation close to the ayah. A short guided question helps the group begin without demanding a long post. Bring one thought to the Circle.

title:
Close with something
you can carry.
caption: A session should end with a clear next step. Use a gentle check-in or shared goal to keep the learning connected after the screen closes. Choose the next return.

title:
An MSA Circle does not
need another group chat.
caption: It needs a focused learning space. Keep Qur'an reading, the shared goal, and check-ins together without unrelated noise. Send this to your MSA exec.

title:
A classroom can learn
without public pressure.
caption: Private participation makes space for quieter students. Use a trusted group format for reading and reflection without likes or followers. Share with a teacher.

title:
A youth group challenge
can stay sincere.
caption: Encourage return without turning worship into a contest. Choose a short Journey and celebrate completion without ranking participants. Plan a seven-day group.

title:
Send an ayah
with intention.
caption: Sometimes one verse brings someone to mind. Share the learning moment privately and let the recipient open the ayah in context. Think of one person.

title: A quiet family check-in.
caption: Read. Reflect. Return. The group can notice that people showed up without demanding everyone write a long message. Keep it light and sincere.

title:
Distance does not have to
end shared learning.
caption: Family and friends can return from different places. A private Circle keeps one purpose visible across busy schedules and cities. Invite someone far away.

title:
Five minutes between
classes can still count.
caption: Open one ayah instead of waiting for a perfect hour. A small reading and reflection moment can fit inside an ordinary student day. Use the next five minutes.

title: Listen on the commute.
caption: Keep the ayah visible while verified recitation plays. Turn travel time into a calm return without leaving the app for audio. Take NIYYAH with you.

title:
Busy season does not mean
losing the connection.
caption: Reduce the size of the action, not its meaning. Continue one ayah, one word, or one reflection when your schedule is full. Choose the smallest return.

title:
Your journal is not
analytics content.
caption: Private spiritual writing deserves stricter boundaries. NIYYAH's product principle is to measure actions without collecting the words you write privately. Privacy should be visible.

title: No public feed required.
caption: Learning together does not need followers or likes. Circles are designed for invited groups and intentional participation. Keep the group trusted.

title:
Created an account?
You can request deletion.
caption: Control should include a clear way to leave. The account area includes a user-facing deletion request flow for signed-in users. Know your choices.

title:
The Qur'an text
is not generated.
caption: Sacred text should come from an established dataset. NIYYAH keeps Qur'an text separate from educational tools and never asks AI to rewrite it. Read the source commitment.

title:
Translation needs
attribution too.
caption: The English wording is a translation, not the Qur'an itself. NIYYAH identifies translation sources so users can understand what they are reading. Check the attribution.

title:
Source tafsir:
only where available.
caption: Coverage is expanding carefully, not pretending to be complete. If an attributed source passage has not been added, the app leaves the source section out. Transparency over appearance.

title: Why I built NIYYAH.
caption: I wanted a calmer way to return to the Qur'an. The goal is not to replace teachers or scholars. It is to help people begin and stay connected. Follow the founder journey.

title:
Building in public means
showing the corrections too.
caption: Trust grows when mistakes are addressed clearly. NIYYAH invites content reports and product feedback instead of pretending the beta is finished. Help us improve.

title:
The beta is a promise
to keep listening.
caption: Real users will shape what deserves attention next. Feedback from students, families, teachers, and Circles matters more than adding random features. Test it honestly.

title: Beta testers wanted.
caption: Especially the people who notice what others miss. Test reading, audio, sources, reflection, Circles, privacy, and accessibility, then report what breaks. Try to break the beta.

title:
MSAs and youth groups:
help test Circles.
caption: We need real group use, not only solo previews. Create a small private Circle and tell us where joining, check-ins, or shared learning feels confusing. Request a group test.

title:
Found one unclear sentence?
That matters.
caption: Content feedback is part of launch quality. Use Report a Content Issue so the team can trace the exact ayah and screen. Send the correction.

title:
Thirty days of showing
what NIYYAH can become.
caption: Now begin with one ayah. The free beta brings reading, listening, reflection, vocabulary, progress, Journeys, and Circles together. Open NIYYAH today.

title:
Your first Circle only
needs two people.
caption: You and someone who helps you return. Choose one short goal, share the invitation, and learn together without public pressure. Create the Circle.

title: The invitation is open.
caption: Understand the Qur'an together. Download the NIYYAH free beta, explore one ayah, and tell us what should improve next. Begin with intention.
